classification.difficultyReason: Infer selection without replacement, reduce the matching category count and total for the second choice, then sum the three same-rating path products.

content.prompt:
In a stack of 10 DVDs, there are 5 rated PG, 3 rated G and 2 rated M.

Grant chooses two DVDs at random from the stack.

Calculate the probability that Grant chooses two DVDs with the same rating.

spec.description: Unlabelled probability branches with first- and second-choice headings. Each first-choice rating branches to PG, G and M in that order.
spec.mathematics: Three first-choice branches and nine second-choice branches; repeated terminal labels are distinguished by their first-choice paths.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied rating labels and stage headings are visible; no probabilities or answers are supplied.

answer.worked:
The DVDs are chosen without replacement.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{PG, PG})&=\frac{5}{10}\times\frac{4}{9}=\frac{20}{90}\\P(\text{G, G})&=\frac{3}{10}\times\frac{2}{9}=\frac{6}{90}\\P(\text{M, M})&=\frac{2}{10}\times\frac{1}{9}=\frac{2}{90}\\P(\text{same rating})&=\frac{20}{90}+\frac{6}{90}+\frac{2}{90}=\frac{14}{45}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Complete probability tree showing the changing second-choice probabilities without replacement.
spec.mathematics: First-choice probabilities PG 5/10, G 3/10, M 2/10. Second-choice PG/G/M probabilities are 4/9,3/9,2/9 after PG; 5/9,2/9,2/9 after G; and 5/9,3/9,1/9 after M.
